analyst_view.overall: Sabah are 30th of 36 with 3 points and Barcelona 8th with 9, so Barcelona need the win to stay near the top eight, while Sabah, in their first Champions League campaign, play in front of a big crowd at the Olympic Stadium in Baku. Barcelona are without Lamine Yamal (ankle), Rodri, Christensen, Espart and Bardghji, all counted by the numbers, and one injury list today also has Kounde and Olmo as doubts; Flick said he will rotate after nine games in four weeks, with Farinas, Eric Garcia, Gerard Martin and Bernal expected in while Raphinha, Pedri, Gordon and Adeyemi still start. Sabah lose defender Aden McCarthy to a red-card ban (counted), and one report today adds forward Mickels as suspended after three yellow cards, which the numbers don't list, plus doubts over Khaybulayev and Simic. Scottish referee Nick Walsh, who gives a lot of cards, is in charge and the numbers already add about a quarter to cards for him.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.4 goals (1.1 Sabah, 3.4 Barcelona), already taking off Yamal (-16.7%), Espart and Christensen for Barcelona and McCarthy for Sabah, and counting both sides' good scoring runs. What they can't see is Flick's announced rotation and, per one report today, Sabah missing forward Mickels through a three-yellow ban, with Khaybulayev and Simic doubtful; together that trims a little from both attacks, so I lean slightly lower, to about 4.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, 6.6 of them for Barcelona, who should have most of the ball against a deep Sabah block. Without Yamal, Barcelona's width comes from Adeyemi and Gordon with Cancelo pushing up, which still sends play down the flanks, and the rotation is mostly in defence and midfield, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, already adding Nick Walsh's high card rate (+26%) and Sabah's busy recent card record (+11%), which fits a side chasing the ball for long spells, and taking a little off for Barcelona's quieter run. That is already a high figure for a game with no rivalry, and nothing new on discipline turned up, so I stay at 5.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.5 shots (8.9 Sabah, 25.6 Barcelona), lifted for both sides' heavy recent shooting. Yamal is one of Barcelona's main shooters and the numbers only take his absence off goals, Flick is rotating, and Sabah may lack Mickels up front, so I lean slightly lower, to about 33.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 shots on target, 9.0 for Barcelona, already lifted for their recent accuracy (+8.5%). Without Yamal and with a rotated side the quality of Barcelona's chances should dip a little, and Sabah's attack is thinner if Mickels is banned, so I trim to about 11.8.
